body:
Godot doesn't do anything special when bundling assemblies during the export process, it uses a standard `dotnet publish` like any other .NET project. So this is likely not a Godot bug.

There's a couple of things that could have gone wrong. Maybe when you added the `Microsoft.Build` or `Microsoft.Build.Locator` dependencies, you didn't configure them properly to be available in a published build. Or maybe you are not using `Microsoft.Build.Locator` as recommended, to ensure the `Microsoft.Build` libraries have been located **before usage**.

Since you didn't include an MRP I can't offer any more guidance than that. Take a look at the [Microsoft documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/visualstudio/msbuild/find-and-use-msbuild-versions) for more information on how to use `Microsoft.Build.Locator`.

However, interestingly, I printed the loaded assemblies during the build process and confirmed that they were correctly loaded. I was also able to access the Create method of ProjectRootElement via reflection. The strange part is that, in the subsequent code, as soon as I call ProjectRootElement.Create(), it throws a "method not found" exception. What's more puzzling is that this issue only occurs after exporting the project.

Bundling `Microsoft.Build` libraries can be tricky. Since this doesn't seem like a Godot issue and there's no MRP, I'll close this issue as resolved.

Please, look at the Microsoft documentation for additional help on how to use the MSBuild APIs:

- [Use the MSBuild API](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/visualstudio/msbuild/msbuild-api)
- [Find and use a version of MSBuild](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/visualstudio/msbuild/find-and-use-msbuild-versions)
- [Microsoft.Build.Locator README](https://github.com/microsoft/msbuildlocator/blob/main/src/MSBuildLocator/README.md)

Do keep in mind that Godot loads your C# project under an ALC, so make sure you are loading the assemblies in the right context:

- [AssemblyLoadContext documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.runtime.loader.assemblyloadcontext?view=net-10.0)
- [How to use and debug assembly unloadability in .NET](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/standard/assembly/unloadability)
